preamble: A velar nasal coda is lost and leaves its nasality on a close front vowel, so a rhyme like -eŋ or -aŋ ends up as [ĩ]. In Southern Min (Hokkien), Middle Chinese -eŋ/-æŋ words have a vernacular reading in [ĩ] in Xiamen and Quanzhou, beside a literary reading that keeps the coda [-iɪŋ]. Zhangzhou and much of southern Taiwan have [ẽ]/[ɛ̃] in the same words.

examples.note: The literary reading keeps the coda: cheng [t͡siɪŋ⁴⁴].
Literary reading chheng [t͡sʰiɪŋ⁴⁴]. Zhangzhou has chheⁿ [t͡sʰɛ̃⁴⁴] instead.
Literary reading seng [siɪŋ⁴⁴]. Zhangzhou has seⁿ [sɛ̃⁴⁴] instead.
